findings.counterexample: Actual source .gitignore is committed into fixture; encode.log is verified ignored and untracked, yet command ref/type/actual byte count/hash still grants qualified PASS.
findings.minimumFix: Authenticate availability of each qualified referenced artifact/record, including nested raw, configuration/booking, sample/compliance/domain/definition and index/result/execution refs. Require committed current-context Git retrieval, or at minimum explicitly reject ignored-untracked referenced files with the existing clean-publication gate; do not rely solely on --exclude-standard. Tracked deliberately force-added .log is valid if actual bytes/hash and scope checks succeed; a blanket extension ban is unnecessary.
findings.noSelfShaLoop: Capture tested code commit/tree first; publish evidence in a later pure permitted evidence commit; source-drift exceptions already support this. Qualified fixture can commit prepared evidence before consumption while retaining old testedSource. No evidence blob needs its own future commit SHA.
findings.scopeLimit: Do not blanket reject legitimate installed/ignored tool dependencies or broaden source/lifecycle exceptions; this check is for referenced qualified evidence and its reproducibility.
